# Command-line reference

**Audience:** operators and integrators. Every command and option of the
`ferrofed` binary, as `ferrofed <command> --help` prints it.
[Configuration](../operate/configuration.md) describes the configuration
every command reads.

<!-- toc -->

## `ferrofed`

```text
The FerroFED openEHR federation gateway

Usage: ferrofed [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  serve        Serves the gateway until the process is asked to stop
  config       Works on the configuration
  admission    Works on the admission of a member (§12b.1)
  conformance  Scores a deployment against the Connectathon tracks of §16.3
  healthcheck  Asks the gateway running on this host whether it is ready, and exits `0` only when readiness answers `200`
  report       Writes the report a complaint or a serious-incident report attaches: the build, the release, the redacted configuration and what the gateway on this host reports, as one archive
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `ferrofed admission`

```text
Works on the admission of a member (§12b.1)

Usage: ferrofed admission [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  check  Creates test EHRs with synthetic subjects on one configured member and reports each identifier-integrity condition of §12b.2 as pass, fail or cannot-check, with its evidence
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `ferrofed admission check`

```text
Creates test EHRs with synthetic subjects on one configured member and reports each identifier-integrity condition of §12b.2 as pass, fail or cannot-check, with its evidence

Usage: ferrofed admission check [OPTIONS] --endpoint <ENDPOINT_ID>

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --endpoint <ENDPOINT_ID>
          The registry endpoint of the member to check

      --count <N>
          How many test EHRs to create on the node, at least two so their `ehr_id`s can be compared, or with `--read-only` the most existing EHRs to read
          
          [default: 3]

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

      --read-only
          Makes no write to the node: reads the `ehr_id` and `system_id` of EHRs it already holds, and names every condition the run leaves unproven

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `ferrofed conformance`

```text
Scores a deployment against the Connectathon tracks of §16.3

Usage: ferrofed conformance [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  run   Drives tracks 1 to 7, 9 and 11 against the configured deployment over ITS-REST and writes the per-track and per-point report (§16.3, §16.4)
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `ferrofed conformance run`

```text
Drives tracks 1 to 7, 9 and 11 against the configured deployment over ITS-REST and writes the per-track and per-point report (§16.3, §16.4).

The run seeds a synthetic patient at every member the cross-reference names, through each node's own ITS-REST writes, and removes nothing.

Usage: ferrofed conformance run [OPTIONS] --patient-namespace <OID> --patient-value <VALUE> --token-file <PATH> --seed-data <PATH>

Options:
      --allow-writes
          Allows the run's writes: a synthetic patient's EHR, the vendored template and compositions, EHRs with no subject, and stored queries

      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --i-understand-this-writes-synthetic-data-to-the-nodes
          Allows a run against a deployment whose profile is not development

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

      --patient-namespace <OID>
          The synthetic patient's namespace, `urn:oid:2.999` or an OID under it

      --patient-value <VALUE>
          The synthetic patient's identifier, which the deployment's cross-reference resolves

      --token-file <PATH>
          A file holding the bearer token the run presents as the caller

      --seed-data <PATH>
          The vendored template and compositions the run writes, checked by their SHA-256: the directory holding them, or the seed data file a release attaches (`ferrofed-conformance-seed-data.json`)

      --gateway <URL>
          The base URL of a gateway already serving the configuration; without it, the run starts the gateway in-process

      --out <DIR>
          The directory the report is written to
          
          [default: conformance-report]

      --node-profile
          Also runs the Federation-Node profile checks and the admission check against every active member and reports their findings as the node profile

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `ferrofed report`

```text
Writes the report a complaint or a serious-incident report attaches: the build, the release, the redacted configuration and what the gateway on this host reports, as one archive

Usage: ferrofed report [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          The TOML configuration file; unset, the product's `_CONFIG` variable names it

      --out <PATH>
          The archive to write, which must not exist yet; by default `ferrofed-report-<UTC time>.tar` in the working directory

      --operator-token-file <PATH>
          A file holding a bearer token with the operator scope, which reads the dependency states and the integrity incidents; without it they are asked with no token

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          One configuration key set over the file and the environment, as `key=value`; repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help
```
